summary: Split worker-rpc into a transport dial plus createWorkerRpcClient(socket) attached through socket.data.handlers; add worker-stream-listener.ts (TCP, bound with the API on worker_stream_port = port + 1) that reads one hello line, resolves the boot token through the single shared lookup CapabilityService.resolveWorkerClaim, answers hello_ack, and registers a WorkerRpcClient by claim token with awaitRegistration(claimToken, timeoutMs); add legion worker-shim --connect tcp://host:port --boot-token-file <path> that dials, spawns OMP only after hello_ack, and reconnects with 200ms→5s backoff replaying gap frames in order. --socket mode is refactored onto a shared bridge with identical wire behaviour.

wireContract.hello: {"type":"hello","bootToken":"<token>"}\n — the first line the shim sends on every (re)connection
wireContract.helloAck: {"type":"hello_ack"}\n — the daemon's only reply to an accepted hello, written before any RPC frame; the shim consumes it and spawns OMP (first ack) or flushes its backlog (every ack)
wireContract.rejection: connection closed, no reply; daemon logs `worker-stream: rejected hello (<reason>)` with reason ∈ {not json, malformed hello, unknown boot token, stale worker generation, already bound to a live stream, hello too long}; no LegionState change
wireContract.afterAck: ordinary NDJSON OMP RPC protocol v2 in both directions, identical to the unix socket (rpc_chunk reassembly, drain-aware writes, run-state tracking shared via createWorkerRpcClient)
wireContract.reconnect: while OMP lives: on drop, redial with min(200·2^n, 5000) ms backoff (n = consecutive failures, reset to 0 by an ack; a close before ack counts as a failure), resend hello, flush the bounded backlog (newest 1000, one drop log) in order after the ack

refinementsToSpec: hello_ack: the daemon answers an accepted hello with one `{"type":"hello_ack"}` line (a second new frame beyond the spec's 'only new frame is hello'); it is what makes 'OMP spawned only after the first successful hello' observable and makes backlog flushing safe.
Rejection reasons add `stale worker generation` (in-memory mint record generation ≠ claim generation, mirroring /worker/started's 409) and `hello too long` (>4096 bytes without newline).
The shared lookup lives in api/auth.ts as CapabilityService.resolveWorkerClaim(state, bootToken) (not api/routes/workers.ts); both /worker/started and the listener call it.
LegionApi gains resolveWorkerBootToken(bootToken) (closure over the private CapabilityService); the listener takes resolveBootToken as an injected function.
DaemonHandle.workerStreamPort and WorkerStreamListener.port are exposed for tests/observability.
Default listener log is console.error with the daemon's `[legion] ` prefix; the injected `log` receives exactly `worker-stream: rejected hello (<reason>)`.
`--boot-token-file` together with `--socket` is a CLI error (would otherwise be silently ignored).
adjacentFindings: worker-rpc.ts and worker-shim.ts decode socket chunks with data.toString('utf8') per chunk; a multi-byte UTF-8 char split across reads becomes U+FFFD in plain (<1 MiB) frames. Pre-existing; fix is TextDecoder({stream:true}); left out because protocol behaviour must stay byte-identical — architect to confirm skipping or assign as fast-follow.
